question: What is the primary reason for Afghanistan's low ranking in the World Happiness Report 2025?

options.text: Economic instability and lack of social support.
High levels of corruption and poor governance.
Worsening conditions for women and societal unrest.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Worsening conditions for women and societal unrest.**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Afghanistan** has been ranked as the **least happy country** in the world in the **World Happiness Report 2025**, a position it has held since the **Taliban** regained power in **August 2021**.

• The primary reason for this record-low ranking is the **drastic restriction of human rights**, particularly the **worsening conditions for women and girls**. The ban on **female education** beyond primary school and the exclusion of women from most **employment sectors** have led to a collapse in societal well-being.

• The report highlights that the **freedom to make life choices** has reached an all-time low in the country, contributing significantly to the overall sense of **societal unrest** and despair.

• While **economic instability** and **poverty** are severe, the systemic **gender-based oppression** and the lack of **social support** systems are the most distinctive factors cited for Afghanistan's unique position at the bottom of the index.

**Additional Information__**

• The **World Happiness Report** is a publication of the **United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)** and uses data primarily from the **Gallup World Poll**.

• The rankings are based on a three-year average of life evaluations. For the 2025 report, data from **2022 to 2024** was analyzed.

• **Finland** continues to hold the title of the **happiest country in the world** for the eighth consecutive year in 2025, followed by other Nordic nations like **Denmark** and **Iceland**.

• The report evaluates countries based on six key variables: **GDP per capita**, **social support**, **healthy life expectancy**, **freedom to make life choices**, **generosity**, and **freedom from corruption**.

• The **International Day of Happiness** is celebrated annually on **March 20th**, the day the report is typically released.
